name: Doximity, Inc.

profile.description: Doximity operates the largest professional network for U.S. physicians and offers clinical workflow tools: secure messaging, the Dialer telehealth app, e-fax, DoxGPT clinical AI search and Doximity Scribe ambient documentation. Most of its revenue comes from marketing and hiring solutions sold to pharmaceutical manufacturers and health systems. FY2026 (March) revenue was $644.9M (+13%) with net income of $196.1M. In fiscal Q1 2027 (June quarter), revenue grew 7% to $156.6M while adjusted EPS fell 19% on heavier AI investment; FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $671-$681M (~5% growth). Co-founded in 2010 by CEO Jeff Tangney; headquartered in San Francisco; market cap ~$5.8B.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Doximity has grown from a physician directory into a workflow platform. The Dialer telehealth app and, more recently, a clinical AI suite (DoxGPT, Scribe, AI Search) opened new revenue: 165 health-system AI clients have signed, and pharma AI Search monetization begins in fiscal Q3 2027 [1][2]. AI Deployment (2/2): The AI products are shipping and in use. Over 75% of Scribe users return weekly, and workflow active prescribers grew more than 30% YoY [2][3]. Market Share (2/2): Doximity is the dominant U.S. physician network, which gives it unmatched pharma reach to verified prescribers [3][4]. Pipeline (1/2): AI Search pharma contracts are guided to fiscal Q3, but OpenEvidence is attacking the same clinical-search and scribe categories, so revenue visibility is only partial [1][5]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2026 R&D of $130.7M was 20.3% of revenue, up from 16.3% a year earlier, top quartile for health information services [6].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Doximity's stated mission of helping physicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients is specific and visibly shapes its free-to-physician product strategy, funded by pharma and health systems [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive, quantified charitable or community program was found. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found. Seven shareholder derivative suits and a new securities class action are a cultural caution flag [7][8]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP Form 4 data show zero open-market insider purchases in 2025-2026 against 7 sales in Q3 2026 and 29 in Q1 2025 (about 7.6M shares), which is clear net selling [9].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically on the Growth-sleeve metrics. The balance sheet is pristine: D/E of 1.1%, ROE of 17.2% (2x weight) and a 25.5% net margin all reach their targets [10][6]. The 5-year revenue CAGR is 25.5% (FY2021 $206.9M to FY2026 $644.9M; 2x weight) [6]. TTM revenue growth has slowed to 7.3%, and forward P/E is 21.0, just over the 20 target. The forward PEG from FMP is -2.85 because consensus expects EPS to fall amid AI spending, so it scores 0 on its 2x weight [10]. Raw weighted score 7.88, which rounds to 8. Liquidity is about $144M of daily traded value.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Doximity's verified network of U.S. physicians and its HIPAA-compliant workflow tools form a real moat. However, AI-native rival OpenEvidence (an estimated ~$150M annualized revenue by November 2025) monetizes physician attention with ads and has expanded into AI scribing and a HIPAA-secure dialer, attacking Doximity's core pharma-marketing model directly [5]. The two companies are suing each other, and Doximity's fiscal Q2 2027 guide of ~1% growth shows the pressure [1][5][8]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Doximity already earns AI revenue, with 165 health-system AI clients signed and pharma AI Search contracts set to start in fiscal Q3 2027 [1].

infinite_game.summary: Doximity is founder-led and built around serving physicians for free, which gives it a genuine cause. Tangney is willing to sacrifice near-term EPS (down 19% in fiscal Q1 2027) to invest in clinical AI. But much of the company's energy is going into a combative, finite contest with OpenEvidence ('we'll win the AI market'), and governance turbulence from securities and derivative litigation weakens the case that it is built to endure.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Keeping physicians' tools free and making doctors more productive so patients get better care is a distinctive, service-oriented cause, and it has guided product decisions since 2010 (free telehealth, free AI scribe) [3][4]. Because pharma advertising funds that cause, it has not been tested across decades or leadership transitions.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management accepted a 19% decline in adjusted EPS and lower free cash flow ($40M vs $60.1M) in fiscal Q1 2027 to fund AI products, choosing long-term capability over margin preservation [1]. The pattern is short and partly defensive against OpenEvidence.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The company remains small (880 employees) and led by its co-founder, which gives leadership continuity [10]. No standout tenure data was found, and the 2025 settlement of a securities suit over disclosure of user engagement ($31M paid by insurers), followed by a new 2026 class action, is a governance caution [7][8].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Doximity has moved from a physician social network to telehealth during COVID and now to a clinical AI suite. These are meaningful but adjacent evolutions on the same physician-network platform and pharma-funded model [2][3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Tangney has said 'we'll win the AI market in 2026', has publicly disparaged the rival's AI, and is engaged in dueling federal lawsuits with OpenEvidence. That framing seeks to defeat rather than learn from a worthy rival [3][5].

investment_thesis: Doximity is a debt-free, very high-margin network (88% gross margin, 25% net margin, 17% ROE) whose free physician tools give pharma and health systems the most efficient channel to U.S. prescribers [6][10]. Clinical AI (Scribe, DoxGPT, AI Search) deepens engagement and has started to monetize, and the raised FY2027 revenue guide of $671-$681M shows the core is holding [1].
thesis_continued: Growth has slowed sharply: about 5% guided for FY2027 and ~1% for fiscal Q2, with EPS declining on AI spend, as OpenEvidence competes for the same physician attention with an ad-funded AI model [1][5]. Litigation (OpenEvidence suits, securities and derivative cases) adds noise [8]. We rate DOCS WATCH: the stock has fallen from a $67 52-week high to ~$33, but we want evidence that AI Search monetization re-accelerates growth before upgrading [10].
key_catalysts: Pharma AI Search contracts contributing revenue in fiscal Q3 2027 [1]
165+ health-system AI clients and >30% growth in workflow active prescribers [1]
Raised FY2027 revenue guidance ($671-$681M) with mid-to-high-80% gross margins [1]
Debt-free balance sheet funding continued buybacks [6]
key_risks: OpenEvidence's ad-funded AI clinical search and scribe directly targeting Doximity's physician attention and pharma budgets [5]
Revenue deceleration to ~1% YoY guided for fiscal Q2 2027 [1]
Securities class action (Michigan Laborers' Pension Fund v. Doximity) and seven derivative suits [7][8]
